### route53-accelerated-recovery-60-minute-rto

**Claim.** Since 2025-11-26 you can turn on accelerated recovery for a Route 53 public hosted zone. It targets a 60-minute Recovery Time Objective (RTO) for making DNS changes again if the US East (N. Virginia) Region becomes unavailable, using a copy of the zone kept in the US West (Oregon) Region, and you must turn it on before any issues with that Region occur. Before it, customers could not modify or recreate DNS records while AWS services in US East (N. Virginia) were unavailable.

**Write it as.** `60-minute Recovery Time Objective (RTO)` · `US West (Oregon) Region` · `2025-11-26`

**Scope.** Route 53 public hosted zones with accelerated recovery turned on; The feature must be turned on before the US East (N. Virginia) Region is impaired..

> "Route 53 accelerated recovery for managing public DNS records helps you achieve a 60-minute Recovery Time Objective (RTO) if the US East (N. Virginia) Region becomes unavailable. When you turn on this feature for a Route 53 public hosted zone, you can resume making DNS changes within about 60 minutes after AWS detects that the US East (N. Virginia) Region is impaired."
> — [Enabling accelerated recovery for managing public DNS records](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/accelerated-recovery.html)

> "When accelerated recovery is on, Route 53 keeps a copy of your public hosted zone in the US West (Oregon) Region."

> "In the past, if AWS services in US East (N. Virginia) became unavailable, customers would not be able to modify or recreate DNS records to point users and internal services to updated endpoints."
> — [Amazon Route 53 announces accelerated recovery for managing public DNS records - AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/11/amazon-route-53-accelerated-recovery-managing-public-dns-records)

> "Posted on: Nov 26, 2025 Amazon Route 53 is excited to release the accelerated recovery option for managing DNS records in public hosted zones."
> — [Amazon Route 53 announces accelerated recovery for managing public DNS records - AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/11/amazon-route-53-accelerated-recovery-managing-public-dns-records)

### route53-accelerated-recovery-data-plane-keeps-answering

**Claim.** DNS query resolution from the Route 53 data plane continues to work normally during Regional service impairment. Accelerated recovery is about regaining the ability to make DNS changes: during a failover, Route 53 routes control plane requests for enabled hosted zones to the US West (Oregon) Region.

**Scope.** Route 53 data plane.

> "It then routes control plane requests for your enabled hosted zones to the US West (Oregon) Region."
> — [Enabling accelerated recovery for managing public DNS records](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/accelerated-recovery.html)

> "Accelerated recovery targets a 60-minute recovery time objective (RTO) for regaining the ability to make DNS changes to your DNS records in Route 53 public hosted zones, if AWS services in US East (N. Virginia) become temporarily unavailable."
> — [Amazon Route 53 announces accelerated recovery for managing public DNS records - AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/11/amazon-route-53-accelerated-recovery-managing-public-dns-records)

> "**Report healthy when all health checks are healthy (AND)** – Route 53 considers this health check to be healthy only when all the health checks that you added to **Health checks to monitor** are healthy."

> "**Report healthy when one or more health checks are healthy (OR)** – Route 53 considers this health check to be healthy when at least one of the health checks that you added to **Health checks to monitor** is healthy."
